messages:
evan: Quick heads-up — Sapphire Cloud returned the quote; procurement flagged a mismatch between our PO payload and their contract template. They can't process the PO until line-item IDs and billing entity map. attaching: sapphire-quote-2026-03-20.pdf
rachel: ugh. Do we have an example of their expected PO shape? @diego @liz
diego: i asked for their EDI/JSON sample earlier, they sent this snippet — here's the mapping they expect:
```json
{
  "vendor": "Sapphire Cloud",
  "billing_entity": "acct_123",
  "lines": [{"sku_id": "SC-GPU-XL", "qty": 10, "unit_price": 3000}]
}
```
liz: our gateway currently emits `payer` and `items[].product_code` — easy to add a mapper but need approval for field normalization + test vector. eng can implement if we get the sample ack window and signer info.
deal-desk: note — Sapphire is also requesting net-90 payment terms and specific indemnity language. they've redlined clause 4.2 (liability). this is outside our standard marketplace terms.
legal-bot: forwarded to contracts team (contracts@). redline file: sapphire_redline_v2.pdf. expected response SLA: 48h. tagging @rachel for priority.
evan: timeline: customer wants onboarding this quarter. if legal takes >48h we lose momentum. options: (1) provisional PO with our standard terms + an acknowledgement clause, (2) manual invoice flow for first month. which is least risky?
rachel: lean towards option 1 to keep them in the flow. @liz can you draft the mapping and a placeholder ack clause we can include in the portal? i'll push contracts for expedited review. :thumbsup:
liz: i can spin up a quick branch and post a demo normalized PO by EOD. will need QA to run through their test harness. tagging @diego for integration tests.
diego: will schedule a 30m sync with Sapphire to validate test vectors — proposing 3pm PT today. sending invites now.
evan: ok thanks all. rachel — keep me posted on the legal thread. if contracts push back hard, we'll do manual invoice for onboarding and hold the marketplace listing until contract is sorted.
